scope: Search for an official, anonymous, bounded-read cadastral parcel polygon source that can return parcel identifiers and geometry for Belgrade. No owner, rights-holder, address, or other private attributes were requested or retained.

authority.name: Republic Geodetic Authority (RGZ)
authority.finding: RGZ describes GeoSrbija as a national platform combining geospatial data, with public map insight into parcel/property information. This confirms the existence of an official public viewing service, not a publicly callable polygon-query contract. The eCadastre page distinguishes public access from a registered service whose use requires an RGZ contract; its result data may include rights-holder name and address and are outside this boundary-only assessment.

catalogSearch.result: The current RGZ organization listing shows five datasets (including address-register and other datasets) but no downloadable parcel-boundary layer. This is scoped to the public listing, not proof no cadastral service or restricted dataset exists.
catalogSearch.openDataPortalNote: Official government announcements identify opendata.geosrbija.rs as an RGZ open-data portal. The confirmed examples found through official listings are the public Address Register and other non-parcel datasets; no anonymous Belgrade parcel geometry endpoint was confirmed.

nearbyGovernmentArcGISCandidate.name: PARCELE
nearbyGovernmentArcGISCandidate.publisherContext: Ministry of Mining and Energy, MiningWaste/kro235 map service
nearbyGovernmentArcGISCandidate.assessment: The REST metadata is reachable and reports a polygon layer with cadastral-looking attributes, but it is a child layer of a MiningWaste service, not an RGZ cadastral publication. Its sublayer extent ends south of central Belgrade (the Belgrade center is north of the reported maximum Y), so it cannot establish a city-wide Belgrade parcel source. Treat it as a topic-specific layer candidate, not a cadastral endpoint. No features were requested.

boundaryVsCadmun: Public records about cadastral municipalities/spatial units are not parcel boundaries. Serbia's Statistical Office describes cadastral municipalities as units in the public Register of Spatial Units, sourced from RGZ; this does not establish the imported SR-cadmun-parcel identifier prefix or prove an anonymous parcel polygon API.

officialEvidence.title: RGZ - GeoSrbija
officialEvidence.relevance: RGZ describes GeoSrbija as the national geospatial platform and says citizens can view parcel/property information.

officialEvidence.title: RGZ - e-Cadastre
officialEvidence.relevance: Distinguishes public search from registered access; registered users need an RGZ agreement. Public property information may include holder name and address, so this audit did not request those attributes.

officialEvidence.title: RGZ - GeoSrbija digital platform announcement
officialEvidence.relevance: Official announcement identifies GeoSrbija as the national platform for finding, connecting, and displaying geospatial data.

officialEvidence.title: RGZ - Address Register
officialEvidence.relevance: Official RGZ page says address-register data are public and available through GeoSrbija/open-data resources. This is address data, not parcel polygons.

officialEvidence.title: Register of spatial units and GIS
officialEvidence.relevance: Official Statistics Office describes cadastral municipalities among its public spatial units and states the data are obtained from RGZ; municipality polygons are not parcel polygons.

officialEvidence.title: RGZ - Javni pristup (Public Access)
officialEvidence.relevance: Public eCadastre allows parcel-number/cadastral-municipality and address lookup, with limited basic property/right-holder information; this is an interactive lookup, not a confirmed feature service.

termsAndPrivacy: Terms are recorded as source context, not an integration gate. Do not use registered/contract-only services or expose owner/right-holder data. No captcha, login, personal-information workflow, or access-control mechanism was bypassed.
decision: Do not enable or propose an executable source descriptor yet. Official cadastral map/data existence is established, but a technically verified anonymous bounded polygon endpoint and its exact native-ID mapping remain unestablished. Because multiple geoportal hosts have repeated connection failures, this result is temporary technical unavailability, not evidence that cadastral maps or underlying source data do not exist.
nextEvidenceNeeded: A successful anonymous small-BBOX response from the current RGZ/GeoSrbija viewer's parcel layer or an official RGZ cadastral feature service.
Layer metadata and field definition that confirm parcel polygons and canonical cadastral parcel IDs, not cadastral-municipality identifiers.
Exact reads for returned native IDs with no missing IDs, duplicate-key conflicts, or geometry conflicts.
